origin: Adding one more decoy option makes another option stand out. It's known from research by Joel Huber and others in 1982, and is also called the asymmetric dominance effect.
whenToUse: You explain how adding an option changes the relative appeal of the existing ones.
whenNotToUse: You'd show false options buyers can't use, or mislead people into a particular plan.

alternatives.name: Compromise Effect
alternatives.reason: Focusing on where the middle option appears.

accessibility: Show each option's price and included benefits as text with the same structure.
